selected.text: Aid me in all conditions to serve Thee amidst Thy creatures. I testify that service unto Thee is naught but the exaltation of Thy remembrance and such deeds as manifest the sanctity of Thy Cause among the peoples of the world.
selected.reason: Defines service through remembrance and deeds that manifest the character of the Cause.

selected.text: To look after the sick is one of the greatest duties. Every soul who becomes sick, the other friends should certainly offer the life (of service) in the utmost kindness.
selected.reason: Makes care of sick people an explicit shared duty.

selected.text: have life, offer up your lives in sacrifice; and so long as ye possess ability, promote learning, crafts, agriculture, and commerce. Recite this blessed verse: "Say: I ask of you no recompense for it
selected.reason: Extends service to learning, crafts, agriculture and commerce without seeking recompense.

selected.text: It beseemeth no one to seek departure from this world in the days of the manifestation of the Lord of Eternity. Rather must all, at all times, be turned toward the horizon of the All-Merciful and beseech God that some service to this most wondrous and impregnable Cause might be manifested from him, even if it be but the mention of one of His words. This, verily, is a great bounty, a great good, and a great matter.
selected.reason: Corrects a wish for departure from life by calling for continued service.

selected.text: Likewise, true beneficence is that thou shouldst be a sign of thy Lord's great mercy, healing every sick one, quenching every thirst, refuge of every lowly one, shelter of every noble one, asylum of every distressed one, and recourse of every impoverished one. This is the righteous deed, the abundant bounty, and the appreciated effort.
selected.reason: Defines true beneficence in a comprehensive set of responses to human need.

selected.text: Dr. Moody and other Americans have forsaken their comfort and migrated from their familiar homeland to render service to all people in Iran.
selected.reason: Historical example of medical workers serving all people across national boundaries.

selected.text: O friends! In such a time, consider the royal favors and sovereign justice as a bounty. Rest not for a moment and seek not an instant's repose. Strive day and night that ye may become the source of such service as will cause the glory of the everlasting government and the comfort and blessing of the poor and the subjects.
selected.reason: Links service in a particular political setting to public welfare and the poor.

selected.text: Today all who have turned to God must occupy themselves with serving one another. Praise be to God that you have been assisted in this, and though you have truly borne hardships in this matter, the recompense thereof is treasured and preserved with God. Every deed performed for God's sake will assuredly receive its compensation both in this world and the next.
selected.reason: Frames reciprocal service as a responsibility for all who turn toward God.

selected.text: The hosts that can render victorious the Truth are goodly deeds and praiseworthy character, and the leader and commander of these hosts is the fear of God. By My life! Few indeed are the ears worthy of hearing this call.
selected.reason: Reinterprets victorious hosts through character, deeds and moral responsibility.

selected.text: He engaged in the service of Thy Cause with utmost dedication, transcribing Thy verses morning and evening until his eyes grew dim and his fingers trembled, his bones weakened and he reached extreme old age. … Yet he never faltered, O my God, for an instant in Thy service, nor did he waver, O my Beloved, for a moment in his servitude to Thee
selected.reason: Memorializes prolonged scribal labor and its bodily cost as faithful service.

selected.text: service to the friends is service to the Kingdom of God and care for the poor is among the divine teachings
selected.reason: Directly links serving friends and caring for poor people to religious teaching.

selected.text: Therefore you should join us in hauling earth and stones at that blessed place - come as soon as possible by whatever means and attain this supreme honor, which is better for you than worshipping both worlds
selected.reason: Values manual labor on a sacred building as a distinctive form of service.

selected.text: It is incumbent upon all to sacrifice self in serving the survivors of those true friends, martyrs in the path of God. Because those birds of the meadows of truth soared to the kingdom of Eternal Might and hastened from this darksome world to the World of Light, but their survivors witnessed looting and plundering, and lost home and security, and are captive in the aggressive hands of the oppressors. These displaced wandering survivors must be cared for with heart and soul and must be served.
selected.reason: Makes support for surviving families of martyrs a concrete obligation.

selected.text: These two groups were both servants of the human world and great benefits came from both classes … This is the essence of divine bestowal, this is grace and mercy that He has enabled you to serve both friend and stranger and made you the manifestation of countless favors
selected.reason: Recognizes different classes of service and benefit to friend and stranger.

selected.text: Let each one of you become the servant of the other; let each sacrifice for the good of other. Do not withhold your lives or your possessions from each other.
selected.reason: Emphasizes reciprocal commitment and sharing resources among companions.

selected.text: Those souls who served the poor during the war years and were in the Red Cross - their services are highly acceptable in the divine Kingdom and the cause of their eternal life.
selected.reason: Explicitly honors wartime Red Cross service to poor people.

selected.text: Truly you strive with heart and soul to render service at the Sacred Threshold. You have no personal motives and seek nothing except God's good pleasure.
selected.reason: Distinguishes sincere service from the pursuit of personal motives.

selected.text: This service of thine is higher than the sovereignty of all the world. This servitude thou dost offer is better than sovereignty over all the world. For earthly power is as vapour in deserted wildernesses, nay worse: it is as deadly venom. But the service thou dost render gives thee lasting sway; it is the rule of high heaven.
selected.reason: Contrasts the enduring value of humble service with temporary worldly rule.

selected.text: Whatever you do, let the people know you are doing it for good, not only to earn you own living. By doing thus you will be able to serve every city to which you go.
selected.reason: Frames earning a living as an opportunity to benefit each city.

selected.text: He is God! Today the foundation of all affairs has been and is service to God's Cause, and it is best for His loved ones in every land to engage in outward affairs, for they can thus convey a word of truth to people or render some service to the friends.
selected.reason: Connects outward occupations with opportunities for truthful speech and help.

selected.text: Thy services have been and are before Our gaze. If one hath drawn a single breath in the path of the Friend, it shall not be lost.
selected.reason: Affirms the value of even a single breath offered in service.

selected.text: During these five years when all nations were drowning in loss and calamity, the free souls, without any lassitude or negligence, have been striving and struggling in that which leads to the life of all and the comfort and tranquility of everyone.
selected.reason: Places work for universal comfort against the losses of wartime.

selected.text: Man must live in the utmost sanctity and purity and he must ever think to assist others and not beg assistance from them.
selected.reason: Raises the relationship between personal self-reliance and assistance to others.

selected.text: During the days of the Blessed Perfection when I got up in the morning the first thing I did was to inquire about the health of all the believers, one by one, and then I called on those who were sick to know how they are. If their indisposition was slight, I treated them myself, otherwise I sent for the Doctor
selected.reason: Offers a concrete daily practice of checking health and securing medical care.

selected.text: And this company stand aloof from selfish imaginings, and, in service to the general good, are ready to lay down their lives. They are the very element of life unto the body of Iran, and in righteous aims they are manifest signs, exerting strenuous endeavor for the reformation of morals, and in the path of the divine good-pleasure they withhold neither heart nor soul. For forty years, despite all afflictions, trials and sorrows, they have labored to reform
selected.reason: Connects selfless service to the general good and social reform.

selected.text: While politics is important in its own right, as are other activities such as trade, industry and agriculture, yet in comparison with the Cause of God, all these matters are playthings of children. Therefore, the beloved of God should busy themselves with the education and nurturing of the human souls so that they may all gather beneath the shadow of the Word of God and assemble under the tabernacle of universal peace and divine love.
selected.reason: Distinguishes spiritual aims from politics and economic occupations while acknowledging their importance.

selected.text: The friends must devote themselves to the development of Iran, that is, they must strive in agriculture, industry, commerce, education and sciences.
selected.reason: Specifies agriculture, industry, commerce, education and sciences as service to national development.

selected.text: If he exerteth effort, it is prompted by naught but the hope of service, and if he undertaketh any business, it is inspired solely by the thought of worship. Therefore, be thou his helper and companion, though thou shouldst lose thereby thy bed and carpet! And in his absence thou art appointed in his stead, to take his place and to devote thyself to service, for thou art trusted of the trusted one of 'Abdu'l-Baha.
selected.reason: Links business motives, worship and service through a personal example.

selected.text: The purpose is the diffusion of divine fragrances and the education of souls and guiding all to that which is the ultimate goal of spiritual ones. For the education of souls is counted among the greatest rewards at the threshold of the Forgiving Lord.
selected.reason: Explains education and guidance as substantive forms of service.

selected.text: How we miss you in carrying soil on the blessed shoulders! … Do not grieve - for a while I carry it by proxy on behalf of Sheikh al-Rais, Afnan, Fadil, Gholamreza Khan, yourself, the Master Builder and other loved ones. selected.reason: Shows shared manual labor and symbolic participation on behalf of absent friends.

selected.text: With unsurpassed humility and fervour, and in a spirit of perfect reverence and devotion, ye have hastened unto the Habitation of Holiness, and in those sacred precincts embosoming the inestimable Gift - the Centre around which circle in adoration the Concourse on high; the Luminous Sepulchre; the Hallowed Spot - ye have with your own hands planted fragrant blossoms.
selected.reason: Presents planting flowers with ones own hands as an act of reverent care.

selected.text: Day and night I gird up the loins of service and seek to bear fruit from the tree of existence. A frame that does not bend in service to the friends is but a prop of wood, and a stature that does not bow under the burden of companions' trials is like the hollow trunk of a fallen palm.
selected.reason: Makes bodily effort and bearing companions burdens part of practical devotion.

selected.text: If thou seekest eternal glory, let thyself be humble and meek in the presence of the beloved of God; make thyself the servant of all, and serve all alike. The service of the friends belongs to God, not to them. … Strive to become a source of harmony, spirituality and joyfulness to the hearts of the friends and the maid-servants of the Merciful
selected.reason: Explicitly joins humility with serving all alike and bringing joy to others.

selected.text: Whosoever is the servant of the believers is the leader of the friends … The service of the friends is service to the True One … Blessed is everyone who serves the friends of God
selected.reason: Defines leadership through service to others.

selected.text: The Apostles labored and gained the means of their livelihood and supported themselves so that they might not be a charge to those who believed in Christ. They were the patterns of sanctity and holiness.
selected.reason: Uses the Apostles livelihood to illustrate supporting oneself while serving.

selected.text: that you are leaving today, and thus, I have come to bid you farewell. In every regard, you have had a wonderful summer, surrounded by the vivifying air of the Shrine of the Bab and its spacious rooms, orchards, flowers and greenery. One must always try to bring comfort and well-being to others; otherwise, bringing comfort to oneself alone is easy and can be readily achieved
selected.reason: Contrasts providing comfort to others with seeking only personal ease.

selected.text: The Cause of God is like unto a college. The believers are like unto the students. The college is founded for the sake of the acquirement of sciences, arts and literature. The students must show the results of their study in their deportments and deeds, otherwise they have wasted their lives.
selected.reason: Develops the college analogy to connect belief, learning and practical conduct.

selected.text: We can all serve in the Cause of God no matter what our occupation is.
selected.reason: Explicitly opens service to people in every occupation.

selected.text: Being thus reduced to utter destitution they went out cheerfully to work and in their turn spent all they made for the maintenance of the poorer Bahai families. Love, yea, love must be demonstrated through deeds. Love has never been a passive verb, a figure of speech; it has always been an active verb, an ideal reality. The sign of true faith is the service of the believers of God and service must always manifest itself in loving deeds and actions.
selected.reason: Shows mutual support continuing even under material destitution.

selected.text: For instance, in our intercourse with others, when you come in constant with another human being, make it's point to discover the condition and needs of that person. He may be in difficulty, suffering for lack of assistance; it should be your privilege to become helpful to him.
selected.reason: Calls for discovering a particular persons condition and needs before helping.

selected.text: "The last generation planted trees that bore fruit for my benefit; so it is now my duty to plant for the benefit of the next generation."
selected.reason: Extends service across generations through planting for future beneficiaries.

selected.text: As long as the ocean surgeth, the sun shineth, and the heaven remaineth lofty and adorned, they must arise with the utmost endeavor to serve. Among the forms of service is wisdom itself, which they must impart to the friends of God, that all may be educated and become the cause of the exaltation of His Cause, rather than the clamor of the heedless and the aggressive.
selected.reason: Offers sustained effort with safeguards against aggressive conduct.

selected.text: Blessed are they who strive to the extent possible to improve your outward affairs and who secretly spend what God hath given them with the utmost humility and submissiveness, that thereby your worldly affairs may be set right.
selected.reason: Commends discreet financial help offered humbly for practical needs.

selected.text: You have truly engaged in service with all your powers and are striving in all directions. You host every arrival and accompany every departure with utmost respect. You constantly spread the feast of hospitality, arrange gatherings of love, prepare celebrations of joy for the friends, and set an abundant table.
selected.reason: Describes the concrete work of welcoming travelers and providing food.

selected.text: Indeed, you rendered many services at this year's Convention and endured hardships beyond your capacity. You traveled before and after the Convention and served through other means as well. You have not a moment's rest. You and your respected wife have dedicated your lives to service to the Kingdom
selected.reason: Records demanding convention and travel work with its personal cost.

selected.text: that they may become the manifestation of "Those who manage affairs … that the consultative assembly may become the manifestation of divine assistance, protection and bounty, that it may be successful in serving the Cause of God, and that they may be loving caregivers to all the friends and think about the comfort, ease, joy and gladness of other friends
selected.reason: Links consultation and administration to the comfort and happiness of friends.

selected.text: Service to the Cause of God consists of detachment and sanctification, abstraction and unity, and the manifestation of merciful attributes among humanity. The fruit and effect of this service is ancient glory for humanity in all divine worlds.
selected.reason: Defines service through spiritual qualities manifested among humanity.

selected.text: the victory of the people of Baha consists in treading the path of guidance, serving the chosen ones, servitude at the threshold of the All-Glorious, carrying out important tasks, and possessing good intentions and benevolence toward all
selected.reason: Joins victory to tasks, good intentions and benevolence toward all.

selected.text: Thou hast been a good means for the harmony of the beloved and this service of thine is accepted in the Kingdom of Abha.
selected.reason: Names restoring harmony as an accepted service.

selected.text: This trustworthiness, religious devotion, firmness and steadfastness that he has shown and continues to show in the affairs of Arbab Jamshid is in truth service to the Cause and evidence of sincerity and servitude at the Holy Threshold.
selected.reason: Treats trustworthy work for another person as religious service.

selected.text: They should certainly always write about the services they are able to render and inform me, so that it may cause spiritual joy and conscious gladness.
selected.reason: Introduces reporting actual services as a form of encouragement and accountability.

selected.text: Seek ye to educate souls and encourage those who attain such virtues. Spread the divine fragrances and to exemplify your beliefs with your conduct and your behaviour as well as your words.
selected.reason: Insists that conduct accompany teaching and education.

selected.text: The greater thine effort in the field of service, the larger the draught thou shalt drink of His life-giving grace. The more thou strivest to serve the friends, the higher wilt thou soar thyself in the realms of the spirit.
selected.reason: Connects helping others with the spiritual growth of the person serving.

selected.text: O my God, make me steadfast in Thy Covenant and cause me to be firm in Thy love, and deliver me from every severe test. My Lord, my Lord! selected.reason: Prays for humility, universal peace, reconciliation and security as purposes of service.

selected.text: he who entertains the desire to live for leadership will in the end be deprived. He will never succeed to serve the Cause of God
selected.reason: Warns that ambition for leadership can defeat the purpose of serving.

selected.text: If one is situated with a family or a number of people who are in need of help and assistance, and one should have tried his best to assist them … Man is responsible to the degree of his power and capacity
selected.reason: Explicitly limits responsibility by actual power and capacity.

selected.text: You must not feel unhappy, because you are not rich. Strive in order to assist the world spiritually. … Consider how many souls have assisted the community with millions yet its result has not been widespread, but those souls who have arisen to guide the people spiritually, their results are unlimited
selected.reason: Explains that lack of wealth need not prevent meaningful spiritual assistance.

selected.text: The friends of God must assist one another in such matters that arise and consider themselves partners in both hardship and ease. Verily He commandeth His servants to righteousness and piety, even as He hath commanded them before in various tablets. Blessed is he who heareth and acteth! Woe unto every heedless and remote one!
selected.reason: Defines mutual support as partnership in hardship and ease.

selected.text: O loved ones of God! Your glory hath not been, nor shall ever be, in slaying souls, but rather in quickening souls that are dead. Strive ye that through the incomparable, flowing waters of the Fountainhead of the Everlasting Lord ye may quicken and give life to dead souls. This is the station of them that love God.
selected.reason: Rejects killing and defines the task as giving life to souls.

selected.text: A hundred thousand blessings upon the soul that hath today arisen to serve the Cause, for service hath degrees and ranks.
selected.reason: Acknowledges degrees and ranks of service rather than a single outward form.

selected.text: This service has been for the sake of God, as it is specially designated for the recreation of the friends and the chosen ones.
selected.reason: Recognizes provision for recreation as service.

selected.text: Arise to assist the Cause to the extent of thy capacity.
selected.reason: Makes capacity an explicit measure of the assistance requested.

selected.text: Thou knowest, O my God, that they desired not corruption in the land nor the shedding of blood. They desired only to illuminate the world with the lights of trustworthiness, chastity, truthfulness and fidelity.
selected.reason: Rejects corruption and bloodshed while naming trustworthy moral conduct.

selected.text: Be thou a light to every darkness, a dispeller of every sadness, a healer for every sick person, a quencher for every thirst, a shelter for every refugee, a refuge for every captive
selected.reason: Includes shelter for refugees and refuge for captives among concrete needs.

selected.text: Today all the people of Iran must strive with the utmost effort and zeal for the good of the government and nation, and with complete truthfulness, honesty and goodwill engage in whatever leads to the prosperity, comfort, wealth and glory of the government and country
selected.reason: Connects truthful work to the prosperity and welfare of the country.

selected.text: Serve all creation without exception, and strive as much as you can to make souls happy and work for the comfort, joy and gladness of all. selected.reason: States the universal scope of service without exception.

selected.text: She believed in You and Your verses, was attracted by Your fragrances, recited Your verses and words, gave glad tidings of the dawning of the Sun of Your divine Oneness, called out Your name in Your kingdom … all out of love for teaching children and passion for educating girls in the farthest lands
selected.reason: Preserves a historical example of dedication to girls education.

selected.text: By day and by night he attended to the flowers and the trees and supplied them with water, even as supplying water to the Sacred Mosque. selected.reason: Honors sustained gardening and watering as work performed in devotion.

selected.text: Become the instrument of the Most Great Peace for all people and promote reconciliation between East and West. As much as you can, bestow the spirit of life and desire comfort and tranquility for the peace of the entire world.
selected.reason: Connects service to reconciliation between East and West and worldwide peace.

selected.text: You strived personally in service to the blessed Cause and girded up the lobes of endeavor and worked personally in building and constructing the school. I swear by the Ancient Beauty that I long for such service, and certainly if I were present I would personally serve among you and work and haul earth, and I would consider this a cause of illumination of my countenance in the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: Records hands-on school construction as educational service.

selected.text: you were engaged in service … Indeed you endured much hardship and showed no shortcoming or laxity. Truly the respected maidservant of God Mrs. Mary Lesch administered with perfect faithfulness, trustworthiness, goodwill and effort
selected.reason: Recognizes faithful administration and the labor of Mary Lesch.

selected.text: All your strenuous efforts in service to the Cause of God, arranging gatherings of fellowship, and striving to free those imprisoned in God's path - all these are remembered and known to God and to this servant, and you are rewarded from His wondrous grace.
selected.reason: Includes efforts to free prisoners alongside fellowship gatherings.

selected.text: You were kinder than a father and truer than a brother! Verily, the service that thou rendered for his sake is a service that thou hast rendered for the Abha Kingdom and is an act of servitude that thou hast manifested for the Sacred Threshold.
selected.reason: Praises personal care that exceeds conventional family obligations.

selected.text: And service consists of purity of intention, abundance of effort, and self-sacrifice in diffusing the divine fragrances and educating the saplings of the divine garden.
selected.reason: Defines service through pure intention, effort and education.

selected.text: you must engage in service in that region, for service to the Sacred Threshold - meaning the diffusion of divine fragrances - is itself pilgrimage, and devotion makes the heart and soul circumambulate the gathering-place of the Concourse on High
selected.reason: Explains how service in ones own region can fulfill the spiritual purpose of pilgrimage.

selected.text: you seek position and rank solely to serve at the Divine Threshold, and you pursue honor and leadership only for the purpose of arising in servitude and protecting and safeguarding the people
selected.reason: Qualifies seeking rank by the sole purpose of serving and protecting people.

selected.text: In the Glorious Gospel it is said: "Freely ye have received, freely give."
selected.reason: Introduces the Gospel principle of giving freely what was freely received.

selected.text: But thou shouldst become a champion in the divine kingdom and a hero of the Lordly Realm so that through the strength of thine arm and the power of thy limbs thou mayest conquer the people of enmity and cause spiritual sovereignty to become penetrative.
selected.reason: Transforms martial imagery into the work of overcoming enmity.

selected.text: Now blessed souls are successful in serving the postal service - they must give thanks, for they are the means for spreading the divine fragrances.
selected.reason: Recognizes postal work as a practical means of communication and dissemination.

selected.text: All your troubles, hardships, difficulties, obstacles and tribulations are evident and clear, and in all these matters I am your partner and share your burden.
selected.reason: Acknowledges hardships while offering partnership in bearing them.

selected.text: Now you must, with the utmost joy and fragrance and infinite gladness, engage in encouraging and nurturing the friends
selected.reason: Names encouraging and nurturing fellow workers as service.

selected.text: during the days of imprisonment you showed the utmost assistance, consideration and support … they strive to serve those imprisoned in the path of God
selected.reason: Records practical support for people during imprisonment.

selected.text: The utmost steadfastness and firmness that you showed in protecting and safeguarding the relatives of His Holiness the Martyr, and your efforts during his absence to prevent, as far as possible, oppression and hostility against those oppressed ones, have caused nearness to the Court of Divine Unity.
selected.reason: Recognizes safeguarding the family of a martyr and assisting the oppressed.

selected.text: Thou hast a sincere intention in service to the divine Kingdom and art assisting thy dear sister that she may engage in service to the Cause of God in Germany. This service is a great bounty in thy behalf.
selected.reason: Recognizes enabling another person to serve as a service in its own right.

selected.text: Strive as much as thou canst to protect and safeguard the dependents of thy deceased brother, for this will draw thee nigh unto the divine court and bring thee close to His threshold.
selected.reason: Makes care for a deceased brothers dependents an explicit responsibility.

selected.text: If it presents no difficulty for you, this would be a service to the Cause.
selected.reason: Preserves a request qualified by whether it creates difficulty for the recipient.

selected.text: To serve the Cause of God in this day is to build the bonds of love amongst the friends of God.
selected.reason: Defines service through strengthening bonds of love.

selected.text: Learn the secret of servitude from 'Abdu'l-Baha, who day and night is engaged in serving the servants of Baha. For servitude unto the one true God can in no wise be attained save through service at the court of His servants.
selected.reason: Expressly links devotion to God with service to His servants.

selected.text: He nurtured the priests and exalted the peasants; he was a refuge to the helpless and a loving, compassionate friend to the distressed.
selected.reason: Includes care for peasants, clergy and distressed people in one example.

selected.text: During the Greek-Turkish war the condition of the Turkish soldiers was frightful … The soldiers showed no gratitude for what they were receiving but on the contrary complained bitterly against their benefactors. Just so we cry out to God, 'have mercy upon us,' when God is the only Giver of Bounty to us
selected.reason: Examines service offered amid wartime suffering and lack of gratitude.

selected.text: Service, social, moral, intellectual service must be the sole aim of a soul. Every Bahai must be a loyal servant of the world of humanity. selected.reason: Names social, moral and intellectual service together with sincerity in professional life.

selected.text: The friends of God must be peacemakers and in matters of common good, promote the general well-being. They must consider Baha’is and nonbelievers as one and the same. We have been created for the betterment of all people and nothing else
selected.reason: Explicitly requires equal concern for believers and nonbelievers.

selected.text: can still distance himself from the things of this world. It would certainly be preferable for him to spend his time in service to the Kingdom of God, but not to practise monasticism. selected.reason: Raises the relation between spiritual service and material obligations.

selected.text: The perfection of man lies in educating, to the extent possible, the children of the poor and others, treating them like one's own children and making absolutely no distinction between them
selected.reason: Requires educating poor children without distinguishing them from ones own.

selected.text: It is better to do both kinds of work unless one is not in need materially, and then one may serve entirely.
selected.reason: Qualifies full-time service by material circumstances and affirms combining kinds of work.

selected.text: These noble people who serve you love you with heart and soul and serve you without any fear, hope or expectation of reward.
selected.reason: Describes assistance without fear, personal hope or expectation of reward.

selected.text: "Assuredly, give to the poor. If you give them only words, when they put their hands into their pockets after you have gone, they will find themselves none the richer for you!"
selected.reason: Insists that help to poor people include material assistance rather than words alone.

selected.text: I am always thinking how to carry the loads of others and not to put my own loads on the shoulders of others
selected.reason: Contrasts carrying others burdens with transferring ones own burdens to them.

selected.text: dedicate the other half in the acquisition of moral virtues and service at the threshold of God
selected.reason: Introduces a concrete division of time for moral growth and service.

selected.text: That which is incumbent today, after recognition, is service to the Cause through wisdom and utterance, and through deeds and character, for goodly deeds and praiseworthy character are the hosts of God, and are mightier than the hosts and armies of earth.
selected.reason: Defines the effective hosts of the Cause as deeds and character rather than armies.

selected.text: Blessed is the soul that hath arisen to serve and is engaged in such deeds and character as befit the Day of God. This Wronged One seeketh helpers, and helpers are deeds from which the fragrance of God can be inhaled.
selected.reason: Explains that the helpers sought are deeds reflecting divine qualities.

selected.text: O friends! Arise with a mighty resolve and powerful determination to serve the Cause, and stand firm. Perchance tyranny, corruption, strife and contention may be eliminated from the world.
selected.reason: Names eliminating tyranny, corruption and contention as the social purpose of effort.

selected.text: O loved ones of the All-Merciful! While time remaineth, strive to make up for what hath passed. Verily He is with you and will aid you in that which befitteth this blessed and wondrous Day.
selected.reason: Offers renewed effort as a way of making amends for past neglect.

selected.text: However, if someone is employed in service to the government for the protection of His Cause or for serving the loved ones of God, there is and has been no objection.
selected.reason: Addresses permitted government employment for protection and service.

selected.text: Blessed is he who is a father to every orphan, a treasure to every poor one, a companion to every stranger, compassionate to every prisoner
selected.reason: Joins care for orphans, poor people, strangers and prisoners in one compact teaching.

selected.text: Thy services and efforts are known and remembered before God. May God willing, thou shalt attain unto His endless bounties. The reward of no one hath been, nor ever shall be, lost before God.
selected.reason: Assures that known or unnoticed effort is not lost before God.

selected.text: Blessed are they who in these days are occupied in service. One deed performed in God's path during these days is dearer and more excellent than the deeds of centuries and ages past.
selected.reason: Explains the distinctive value attributed to action in this Day.

selected.text: Make your deeds for God, and your call in His Name, and your orientation toward His horizon
selected.reason: Centers intention, speech and direction on God.

selected.text: The loved ones of God, who have appeared solely for the reformation of the world, have been reckoned among the corrupt.
selected.reason: Records the painful discrepancy between reforming aims and accusations of corruption.

selected.text: The purpose is this: Praise be to God, the Afnan, the branches of the Blessed Tree, are steadfast in the Cause and constant in the remembrance of the Ancient Beauty. They have no purpose save the spreading of the divine fragrances, and no desire except the exaltation of God's Word, for the obligation upon the branches of the Sacred Tree is different.
selected.reason: Distinguishes particular family responsibilities from general obligations.

selected.text: Thou art helping the helpless ones and art comforting those who are insane.
selected.reason: Specifically includes compassionate care for people with mental illness, retaining source terminology.

selected.text: I became very pleased and satisfied with him that he serves the wounded soldiers in the hospital with perfect sincerity of intention and effort, and in London he is truly a faithful and steadfast servant to the wounded soldier. O a thousand praises upon him for being a true Baha'i and therefore engaging in this work - truly he is serving God.
selected.reason: Recognizes hospital service to wounded soldiers as service to God.

selected.text: Observe how 'Abdu'l-Baha in such a storm has completely forgotten himself and arisen to protect and preserve the friends. He has sent most of the friends to other regions, and at such a time and in such a state and such danger, how difficult and hard such work is.
selected.reason: Describes concrete protective action and relocation of friends in danger.

selected.text: The greatest service is the firmness of the chosen ones, the unity and oneness of the faithful, the agreement of hearts, the connection of souls, unity of word, and the teaching of the Cause of God
selected.reason: Integrates steadfastness, unity of hearts and teaching as forms of service.

selected.text: Your services at present are similar to the sowing of seeds by the farmer in the field. It is impossible for germination to occur immediately. Therefore, the farmer must be very patient and not become disheartened. He should continue with his work, knowing that the day will come when the harvest appears.
selected.reason: Explains delayed results through the patient work of sowing and harvesting.

selected.text: Help them to learn the ways of servitude to the Threshold of the Exalted One, and impart to them the lesson of relationship to the Illumined Court. In brief, in the school of the wondrous Faith become a learned teacher to the handmaidens of God enabling them to educate their children
selected.reason: Links assisting mothers with their ability to educate children.

selected.text: Give great importance to the matter of the poor - be a refuge and shelter to every poor one, and a protector and helper to every sick one. Be self-sacrificing in the path of the destitute and become a secure cave of shelter for the needy, so that you may witness the aid and favors of Baha'u'llah from the Most Glorious Horizon and attain the greatest gift.
selected.reason: Gives explicit priority to poor and sick people.

selected.text: In any case, you must succeed in rendering such service as befits this title, otherwise you too, like me, will have a name without reality in the realm of possibility
selected.reason: Requires conduct to give reality to a claimed title.

selected.text: I hope he will be assisted and confirmed in this invention and render a service to the human world.
selected.reason: Includes useful invention among services to humanity.

selected.text: Give thanks to God that you were enabled to serve the Cause of God and assisted with the printing of treatises and collectively engaged in service
selected.reason: Recognizes printing and collective production of writings as service.

selected.text: Regarding Ahmad Maqsud, the intention was that perhaps he could provide some assistance to his father, since due to having many dependents he is in utmost distress, and to the extent possible consideration should be shown to him in this matter. If something could be arranged that would bring happiness to his father, it would be most appreciated.
selected.reason: Addresses assistance to an overburdened father with many dependents.

selected.text: She never wavered in serving Thy loved ones and comforting Thy servants … She spent her wealth upon the weak and the poor … She was a treasure to every poor one, a shelter to every captive, a refuge to every stranger
selected.reason: Memorializes a woman whose wealth supported poor people, captives and strangers.

selected.text: this service that you render - teaching the tender young plants in the garden of the love of God with utmost effort in science and culture, instructing them in spiritual qualities, and teaching them proofs and evidences
selected.reason: Combines science, culture, spiritual qualities and reasoned teaching in education.

selected.text: Assist Thy servants Hassan and Hussein for the noble endeavors they showed in shrouding that truthful servant, washing his purified body, and burying him with resolute determination
selected.reason: Honors washing, shrouding and burying the dead as concrete acts of care.

selected.text: your purpose is to serve the Cause of God, not to praise or criticize individuals
selected.reason: Distinguishes serving a shared purpose from praising or criticizing personalities.

selected.text: Whosoever ariseth further, shall obtain a greater share; and the valiant hero who urgeth ahead and hit the polo ball of service, will carry off the prize, and it maketh no difference whether man or woman, whether male or female.
selected.reason: Explicitly states that achievement in service does not depend on being male or female.

selected.text: Your respected father hath exerted his utmost efforts and hath served the Faith of God all this time. Now your turn hath come to be the cause of his happiness and comfort
selected.reason: Recognizes the responsibility to provide happiness and comfort to a father after his years of service.

selected.text: God hath blessed the human reality with two stations: one is the state of being which seeks to acquire perfections, the other is that which craves to share these perfections with others. In other words, seek not only to acquire these bounties from the Kingdom but proffer them freely to the children of men.
selected.reason: Explains the complementary movements of acquiring perfections and freely sharing them.

selected.text: so that thou mayest spend thy life in healing both stranger and kin, and dedicate thy precious time to curing the diseases of both rich and poor
selected.reason: Directs medical care equally to strangers and relatives, rich and poor.

selected.text: You had asked about service - act according to the divine teachings and always keep the heavenly counsels before your eyes. This is service to the Cause of God
selected.reason: Answers a direct question about service with the practice of divine teachings.

selected.text: We feed you for the sake of God alone. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.
selected.reason: Uses the Quranic refusal of reward or thanks to explain generous motives.

selected.text: I prayed in behalf of all the family that they may be confirmed with the most great guidance and sacrifice their abilities, talents and possessions in the Path of God.
selected.reason: Includes abilities and talents alongside possessions as resources to offer.

selected.text: Thou hast complained of being deprived of the company of the friends but when thou art engaged in serving thy mother and other relatives, this too is obedience to the command of God. This too will cause thee to attain the good pleasure of God.
selected.reason: Affirms that caring for a mother and relatives is obedience even when it limits community participation.

selected.text: The effort you made in paying the debt of Bashir-i-Ilahi was a distinguished service, accepted and evident at the Divine Threshold.
selected.reason: Recognizes paying another persons debt as a particular act of service.

selected.text: there is no better work than for a person to become the cause of comfort, ease and livelihood for the friends of God
selected.reason: Names enabling livelihood, comfort and ease as valuable work.

selected.text: service to the Cause means to acquire divine characteristics and to hold fast to the Most Firm Handle of the Absolute Truth. This means manifesting praiseworthy qualities and being adorned with holy attributes, being enkindled with the fire of God and being attracted to the perfuming breaths of God
selected.reason: Defines service through acquiring divine characteristics and praiseworthy qualities.

selected.text: Whenever you find time and travel to different areas, and inspire each of the loved ones of God with a breath of joy, it is very acceptable and beloved at the divine threshold
selected.reason: Qualifies travel for encouragement by available time.

selected.text: The friends of God assembled together with rejoicing and conveyed the stones themselves, upon their backs, while attracted by the love of God and for the Glory of God.
selected.reason: Shows a community sharing the physical labor of carrying building stones.

selected.text: Thank ye God that in Hamadan in the school founded by the Baha'is ye have become teachers and Professors
selected.reason: Recognizes teachers and professors working in an established school.

selected.text: "How can I raise my head in shame before the Friend, when no worthy service has come from my hand?"
selected.reason: Preserves a poetic expression of self-examination about the worth of ones service.

selected.text: The purpose is that the Spiritual Assembly should serve the friends with the utmost spirit and joy
selected.reason: States that the purpose of the Spiritual Assembly includes joyful service to the friends.

selected.text: The best of undertakings is to gather together every Sunday to expound upon the pure and goodly life and universal brotherhood which reveal the philosophy of universal religion
selected.reason: Specifies recurring gatherings devoted to good living and universal brotherhood.

selected.text: of the All-Merciful! Thou didst protect a believer and show kindness to an illustrious soul, delivering him from the hands of oppressive adversaries
selected.reason: Records protection and rescue from oppressive adversaries.

selected.text: Today whosoever is engaged in the service of the Cause of God he is like a gardener who is planting a tree. Ere long that tree shall grow and develop, giving cool shade to all parts and producing most luscious fruits. Therefore thank thou God that thou art confirmed in the service. Exert thou day and night so that thou mayest add to thy services.
selected.reason: Develops the growing-tree image for the delayed fruits of service.

selected.text: This sincere intention that you have is itself service, and assuredly you will be assisted to servitude before the Blessed Beauty
selected.reason: Affirms the value of sincere intention when action is still being sought.

selected.text: Should I fall short, you shall complete the task; should I falter, you shall press forward. When two weak frames are made to stand firm in a single purpose, they acquire the strength of one mighty frame. Perhaps through divine assistance and grace we shall accomplish something in servitude.
selected.reason: Shows two people compensating for one anothers weakness through shared purpose.

selected.text: The victory of God is the guidance of the people, servitude at the Threshold of the Almighty and wholehearted devotion to the advancement of the cause of the oneness of the human world.
selected.reason: Defines victory as guidance and advancing human oneness.

selected.text: Today, at the Threshold of His Holiness Baha'u'llah, there is nobody more favored than thee, because thou art busy in the service of the orphans and in the education of the destitute, helpless children. Thou hast no desire but to please God. … Verily, verily, this service is directly rendered to His Holiness Baha'u'llah Himself, because these children are His dear children
selected.reason: Explicitly identifies care and education of orphans with service to Bahaullah.

selected.text: O lion of the field of sacrifice! The excellence of beasts of prey lies in their ferocity, sharp claws and fearlessness. But the lions of the jungle of divine knowledge are distinguished by their freedom from attachments, their generosity, their servitude and their oneness.
selected.reason: Contrasts animal ferocity with spiritual courage expressed in generosity and unity.

selected.text: In this day service at the sacred Threshold of the Blessed Beauty and steadfastness in the Cause of His love is the real sacrifice of the self. God willing thou shalt attain this service through all its grades and conditions.
selected.reason: Interprets sacrifice of self as service and steadfastness.

selected.text: this - while all the people on the ship are peacefully asleep in their beds, embraced by comfort, this sick one, captured by love for the friends, has been occupied with writing from sunrise until now, that perhaps it may bring solace to hearts and joy to souls
selected.reason: Preserves the historical setting of correspondence written while ill aboard ship.

selected.text: Among other things, he can engage in service, establish bonds of fellowship with everyone, and with the utmost spirituality make strangers into friends.
selected.reason: Names making strangers into friends as a practical outcome.

selected.text: True bounty belongs to him who draweth forth his hand from out the sleeve of the love of God so as to bestow upon the world and all its peoples the favours borne of the holy and sanctified perfections of the Lord.
selected.reason: Defines generosity as sharing divine perfections with all peoples.

selected.text: What is hoped for is the exertion of loyal effort in completing this lengthy case. When this is accomplished, it will leave an influence that shall endure throughout ages, centuries and epochs.
selected.reason: Recognizes patient completion of a lengthy case as lasting service.

selected.text: A tree is of no service to any one on the summit of a mountain, but should stand in a place where it will give shade and where its fruits can be gathered.
selected.reason: Uses an accessible fruit tree to explain placing ones capacities where others can benefit.

selected.text: Consider thy composure, for composure of thought will become the cause of one's confirmation in the service.
selected.reason: Connects composure of thought with effective service.

selected.text: It is my hope that extraordinary souls in that country from among the people of that country will arise in service.
selected.reason: Calls for people native to a country to arise in service there.

selected.text: Thou shouldst continue thy profession and at the same time try to serve the Kingdom of God
selected.reason: Explicitly counsels continuing a profession while serving the Kingdom.

selected.text: I hope that from the Court of the One you will be enabled to serve your parents with utmost strength. Those two helpless ones have truly faced severe hardships. May you become the cause of arranging means for their comfort, and likewise be assisted in educating your brothers that they may receive divine training and learn heavenly manners.
selected.reason: Brings care for suffering parents and education of children into one instruction.

selected.text: Every blessed soul who assists the Baha'i schools, or who opens hand and heart to their progress and strives for their organization, will receive praise from the Concourse on High and become a recipient of the effusions of the Abha Kingdom
selected.reason: Includes organizing and supporting schools alongside teaching.

selected.text: Thanks be unto Thee that we have been rendered successful in offering this service, and have been confirmed in this bestowal. Although we are destitute, yet we are striving towards laying the foundation of this great temple.
selected.reason: Shows collective temple-building undertaken despite poverty.

selected.text: In Yazd, the Spiritual Assembly is charged with comforting, inquiring after and serving the kindred of the martyrs. Until now, whatever was necessary has been sent from various quarters. Now too, quickly inform us of whatever is needed so we may attend to it.
selected.reason: Assigns an Assembly to inquire into bereaved families needs and report unmet requirements.

selected.text: Let those friends, in return for this blessed journey, assist to the extent possible the poor and weak from among all the peoples of the world, that it may be acceptable in every way.
selected.reason: Links a blessed journey with practical help for poor people of every people.

selected.text: a love that is always ready to sacrifice, which does not demand but gives, which does not exalt itself or put itself above others, but which sacrifices itself even to the lowliest of beings, which helps to carry the burdens of the fellow-disciples, shares their battles and seeks to dry their tears
selected.reason: Describes love that gives without demanding, shares struggles and dries tears.

selected.text: They have to serve the worshipers of God, for He (praise to Him!) is not in need of our service, our submissiveness or prayers, our kindness or assistance, etc., but those who are in need of such things are the worshipers of God, and by this they will please God the Almighty.
selected.reason: Explains why service reaches people: God does not need human assistance.

selected.text: His most important service in the Cause was to carry the Tablets of Baha'u'llah to the believers of Persia and bring back to Him their petitions. Thus he travelled back and forth between Persia and Acca, being for years the sole channel of correspondence between the Blessed Perfection and the friends.
selected.reason: Preserves the demanding historical work of carrying letters and petitions.

selected.text: The Sisters of Mercy, although nuns, serve the people with the most unselfish spirit. They teach the children, nurse the sick, make the poor self-supporting and do many other useful services.
selected.reason: Recognizes the useful work of the Sisters of Mercy across religious difference.

selected.text: O friends! We must do something for the edification of His Cause. We must exert to water this Divine Tree. We must bid farewell to all ideas save the focal idea of Service. We must learn and grow and expand and develop.
selected.reason: Connects service with learning, growth and development.

selected.text: man must be the cause of prosperity, not destruction. God created man upon this sphere that he might be the cause of its development. Man must strive for prosperity. The more he labors for the flourishing of this world, the more acceptable is he in God's sight
selected.reason: Defines the human task as developing and prospering the world rather than destroying it.

selected.text: Seek health so that you may succeed in rendering service. … The results of health are good for mankind, they are very great, if spent in what is proper and fitting
selected.reason: Explicitly encourages seeking health in order to serve effectively.

selected.text: If we are not going to be conducive to the glory of the Cause, we must not at least be the means of its debasement. If we are not willing to serve at His Holy Threshold we may not at least through our actions contribute towards its disgrace. If we cannot become the means of union we may not create causes of difference and disruption.
selected.reason: Sets a minimum safeguard against harm, division and debasement when active help is lacking.

selected.text: You must help the poor. Help the orphans. You must nurse the sick people. You must treat all alike, whether believers or enemies of the Cause; Bahais or non-Bahais. In helping, give to all alike, or in making any great sacrifice, it must be the same, whether to a Bahai or not--make no difference. Try to educate some children.
selected.reason: Extends equal practical care even to enemies of the Cause.

selected.text: memory. He has memorized ever so many Tablets! Every faculty of the faculties of man which is used in the path of the Blessed Perfection is like the oil which burns in this lamp - illumining this room;- whether it is the faculty of memory or the power of speech or the art of music and song or the gift of writing or the talent of painting or the endowment of poetry etc, it will produce infinite results
selected.reason: Includes poetry and other individual faculties among resources for service.

selected.text: He amongst you who desires to become first must be the last, and he who desires to be a master, must become a servant … Ye must be a servant to all. Ye must serve with heart and soul in utmost humility and submission
selected.reason: Connects serving a meal with the Gospel reversal of mastery and service.

selected.text: I helped him to unload his donkey and then quietly we sat under the inviting shade of a tree. Then he began to play with such depth of feeling and beauty that my whole heart went to him. I drank deeply the sweet cadences and harmonies of his flute to such an extent that I was entranced thereby. … When he finished playing I assisted him again to load his donkey, gave him a present and the address of our house and asked him to call on me next day
selected.reason: Shows attentive everyday help and appreciation for a musicians gift.

selected.text: You can offer services in English, and in America you can offer a better service in English. One of the most appropriate Utterances of Baha'u'llah while He was in the City of Adrianople is this : 'If your word concerns GOD it is good be it spoken in Hebrew or Syriac. If you seek GOD it is good whether you come to Him in one place or another.' Therefore, his honor, Mr. --- will do well when he does a thing for GOD be it in English or Persian
selected.reason: Affirms effective service in the language a person actually knows.

selected.text: If they sleep they must sleep with the idea of being refreshed;- so that when they arise next morning they may serve the Cause with greater efficiency and strength. If they eat they must eat with the object of building up new life-force, in order that they may move and walk in the Celestial Highway.
selected.reason: Explains sleep and refreshment as preparation for more effective work.

selected.text: All the Christians left their homes and fled, entrusting the protection of their households to us. They made a request, and through the government we appointed thirty people to patrol the Christian quarter at night and protect it.
selected.reason: Records protection of Christian households during danger.

selected.text: On my way, there was a deep stream with strong current. As I was passing by I heard the cry of a man for help and when I looked around I saw a camel in the stream trying to save himself and the owner was standing by helpless … They brought the cords and with it tied the feet, the tail, the neck of the camel but they could not save it
selected.reason: Includes a narrative of attempting to rescue an animal in distress.

selected.text: He must look upon his position as a sacred trust not be bought by the plutocrats and so called captains of industry. He must divest himself from any prejudice and his aims must be altruistic and advantageous to the whole community. … He must believe consciously that he is the real servant of the public and not their overbearing lord. He must serve all, irrespective of any personal predilection or inclination
selected.reason: Treats public office as a sacred trust insulated from wealth and personal prejudice.

selected.text: In fact, a number of the soldiers, that is, those who were ordered to guard us, were very sick and I began treating them at once.
selected.reason: Describes medical care offered to the soldiers guarding the prisoners.

selected.text: Join yourselves to those who work for the poor, the weak and the unfortunate; this is greatly to be commended.
selected.reason: Encourages joining others who already work for vulnerable people.

selected.text: Of what use is it that we know for a fact there are ten thousand people cold and hungry if we do not feed and warm them?
selected.reason: Contrasts merely knowing about hunger and cold with feeding and warming people.

selected.text: and not be based upon passion and desire. In the latter case, they might live together for a few years, but afterwards, differences may arise... Each should seek to comfort and assist the other
selected.reason: Applies mutual comfort and assistance to married life.

selected.text: I wish to come up to the pilgrim house and cook a pot of bulgur pilaf for the friends. The Blessed Beauty has appointed me as a servant of the beloved ones, therefore I must occasionally arise to fulfill this duty.
selected.reason: Shows cooking a meal as a personal expression of service.

selected.text: They are serving the Cause of God, not for name, fame and winning glory. Not simply because their sense of duty is strong, but a duty which is permeated with pleasure and joy.
selected.reason: Distinguishes joyful duty from pursuit of fame and recognition.

selected.text: Indeed, the person mentioned was peerless in the science of cultivating palm trees and their offspring, as evidenced by clear and manifest proof, namely that his service was rendered in such a station that every knowledgeable scholar and wise sage would testify to it, both outwardly and inwardly. Glory be to God! As his deeds were for the sake of God, they illumined the world of deeds at this station.
selected.reason: Recognizes skilled cultivation of palms as a distinctive practical contribution.

selected.text: O servants of the All-Merciful! Ye have been created for the advancement, prosperity, and exaltation of those who dwell on earth. Occupy yourselves with that which befitteth the station of man.
selected.reason: States advancement and prosperity of all earths inhabitants as a purpose of human existence.

selected.text: Furthermore, the trouble of your eminence's attention in seeing the sugar and tasting its flavor, and attention to other troubles, and sending of trusts which are considered among the great services, and other various attentions which cannot be limited by the pen - all are mentioned and their rewards are beseeched and hoped for from God, exalted be His station.
selected.reason: Recognizes careful attention to provisions and entrusted goods as practical service.

selected.text: If what was mentioned is acted upon, that is, if your honor arises to assist the oppressed, God, exalted be His glory, will surely, with the ocean of generosity and heaven of bounty, grant a complete reward
selected.reason: Makes active assistance to the oppressed the response required of the recipient.

selected.text: Remain firm and steadfast in all things and conditions in the Cause of God, the Resplendent, the Impregnable, and carry out the services to the Cause to whatever extent possible through hand, tongue, heart, soul and spirit
selected.reason: Names hand, tongue, heart, soul and spirit while qualifying effort by possibility.

selected.text: Know thou with clear certainty that thy existence and continuance in service to the Cause is better than what thou hast chosen for thyself and desired from thy Lord.
selected.reason: Affirms continued life in service over the recipients wish for departure.

selected.text: All have been created for attainment unto His presence; however, today service to the Cause takes precedence. Whoso is assisted today to aid the Cause, verily he hath attained unto all good from God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Gives service priority over a desire to attain physical presence.

selected.text: the time when the servant of God came to him in days of hardship and sought his protection, and he protected him. By God, this good deed was better than the worship of those who worshipped their Lord for months and years
selected.reason: Ranks protecting a vulnerable person above prolonged acts of worship.

selected.text: These are the hands of God's Cause amongst His servants and the dawning-places of the suns of knowledge in His lands. The might of the heedless hindereth them not, nor doth the clamor of the aggressive turn them aside from their purpose. Their concern hath been and is the betterment of the world and the salvation of nations.
selected.reason: Connects learned service with betterment of the world and salvation of nations.

selected.text: It behooveth all to attend, according to their means, to his affairs. This is among the conditions of faith and certitude, of love and unity.
selected.reason: Makes collective care for a particular person proportional to peoples means.

selected.text: Consider ye the oppressed, the distressed, the hungry, the naked, the weak and the poor. Thus doth your Lord, the All-Merciful, command you
selected.reason: Directs attention explicitly to oppressed, hungry, unclothed, weak and poor people.

selected.text: grant her the privilege of serving the Dayspring of Thy Cause in the worlds which Thou hast ordained
selected.reason: Extends the prayer for service into the worlds beyond this life.

selected.text: All in the world, whether male or female, have been created for the recognition of God, the remembrance of God, and service to His Cause.
selected.reason: Explicitly gives women and men the same purpose of recognition, remembrance and service.

selected.text: and hast wrought with thine own hands for God that which is better for thee than all the ornaments of earthly dominion
selected.reason: Honors work performed with ones own hands above material adornment.

selected.text: Blessed is he who beareth burdens but causeth none to bear his own.
selected.reason: Offers a concise teaching on bearing burdens without burdening others.

selected.text: Today is the day of deeds and not of words, and their deeds are a truthful witness and faithful testimony to their love, detachment and service.
selected.reason: Makes deeds the credible evidence of professed love and service.

selected.reference: LG#1835, M63-86 375.5 (1 Sep. 1983 on behalf of the Universal House of Justice)
selected.text: Baha'u'llah has stated quite clearly in His Writings the essential requisites for our spiritual growth, and these are stressed again and again by 'Abdu'l-Baha in His talks and Tablets. One can summarize them briefly in this way: 1) The recital each day of one of the Obligatory Prayers with pure-hearted devotion. 2) The regular reading of the Sacred Scriptures, specifically at least each morning and evening, with reverence, attention and thought. 3) Prayerful meditation on the teachings, so that we may understand them more deeply, fulfil them more faithfully, and convey them more accurately to others. 4) Striving every day to bring our behaviour more into accordance with the high standards that are set forth in the teachings. 5) Teaching the Cause of God. 6) Selfless service in the work of the Cause and in the carrying on of our trade or profession. These points ... represent the path towards the attainment of true spirituality that has been laid down by the Manifestation of God for this age.

selected.reference: LG#405 (12 Jul. 1952 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi)
selected.text: There is nothing that brings success in the Faith like service. Service is the magnet which draws the divine confirmations.
